example: a tiny decoder-only GPT trained here from scratch: d_model 256, 6 layers, 8 heads of 32, context 256, learned positions, a GELU FFN of width 1,024, pre-norm LayerNorm and tied embeddings, 5,836,032 parameters (4,721,920 outside the embeddings). It trains on TinyStories (CDLA-Sharing-1.0; one shard of 122M tokens) with its own byte-level BPE of 4,096 tokens, 1,500 steps of 8,192 tokens (12.3M tokens, about 5 minutes on the laptop's GPU), and reaches a held-out loss of 2.30 (2.16 with RoPE instead of learned positions, the setting the attention runs use). The running sequence is 256 tokens of a held-out story, Roxy the rhinoceros and the icy hill, never seen in training; names repeat ("Roxy" 11 times), which attention, copying and cache demos need. measured.
example_open: SmolLM2-135M (Apache-2.0, Hugging Face revision 93efa2f0; 30 layers of width 576, 9 query heads and 3 KV heads), run on the same story re-tokenised with its own tokenizer (226 tokens), with Qwen3-0.6B (Apache-2.0, revision c1899de2) as a second opinion.
tiny_shapes: d_model 256, 8 query heads of 32 with 8 KV heads (full multi-head attention), an FFN of 1,024 with GELU (two matrices), no biases: 786,944 weights per block, 262,144 in attention and 524,288 (two thirds) in the FFN, the classic 4d² and 8d² split; six blocks, the tied 4,096 × 256 embedding and the 256 learned positions make 5,836,032 measured (model.param_groups()).
attn_variants: held-out loss after 1,500 steps of 8,192 tokens (RoPE in every preset, 100 validation windows): MHA 2.160 (6,144 bytes of cache per token in BF16), GQA-4 2.185 (3,072), GQA-2 2.182 (1,536), MQA 2.177 (768), MLA 2.255 (960), sliding window 64 2.173 (at most 64 tokens per layer), and 2 local : 1 global layers at window 64 2.154, slightly ahead of full attention measured. A second seed moved MHA by 0.016, so the grouped variants cost nothing measurable at this size; MLA is about 0.1 worse (seed 1: 2.248), which does not reproduce DeepSeek's result (the Attention lab discusses why). The decode step is a memory-traffic story: one attention layer of Llama 3.1 8B's shape with 32K cached tokens (batch 4, on the laptop's GPU) takes 0.34 of MHA's time with GQA-8, 0.09 with MQA and 0.20 with absorbed MLA, against cache bytes of 0.25, 0.031 and 0.070 measured: the ratios follow the bytes; the milliseconds do not transfer to a datacenter GPU.
sink: under 0.09 of the attention lands on the first token in layers 0 to 11, and 0.31 to 0.74 from layer 12 on, the layer where one dimension of the first token's residual stream jumps to about 20,000 (section 7). Masking the first token as a key in every layer raises the loss on the running text from 1.563 to 1.648 and derails generation ("Once upon a time, and the people were so much in love with him, that they would not let him go out of the house."). On 1,024-token stories a 64-token sliding window without the first token doubles the loss after the window (3.36 against 1.62); keeping just the first token brings it back to 1.81 measured. The tiny GPT, trained on 12.3M tokens, has no sink: at most 0.05 on the first token in any head. Inside a real model has the maps.
prepost: at the default learning rate 3e-3 with a 100-step warmup, post-norm never leaves the unigram plateau: it ends at 5.943, the loss of predicting each token by its frequency (6.006), while pre-norm reaches 2.281 with identical settings; the gradient reaching its first block is 5.1e-7, against 0.27 for the same post-norm model trained with a 500-step warmup and 0.92 for pre-norm at 1e-3. With that longer warmup post-norm trains and reaches 2.138, the best of the eight runs; at 1e-3 it reaches 2.534. Pre-norm trains at every rate tried, degrading to 4.361 at 3e-2. The residual stream shows the cost of pre-norm: its median norm grows from 1.3 after the embedding to 46 after the first block and 65 after the sixth, while post-norm (at 1e-3) holds it near 16, √256, through every block until a last jump to 25 measured. The Block lab draws both.
massive: dimension 507 of the first token's residual stream reaches 20,156 at layer 12 and stays above 4,047 to the last block, while the median entry at that depth is about 1.6, a ratio near 13,000 to 1; Qwen3-0.6B shows the same thing, dimension 35 of the first token at 6,160 in layer 26, about 1,100 times its median measured. The tiny GPT, without a sink, has none: its largest entry after training is 36.
cfg_check: rechecked on 2026-10-19 against the saved config.json files (src/data/configs) and the Config calculator: 43 values agree, including every row of this table, Llama 3.1 70B and 405B, DeepSeek-V3, gpt-oss-120b, Gemma 3 27B, Qwen3-Next and SmolLM2-135M (src/read/derive.py).
calc_resid: the Config calculator reproduces the Hugging Face stored-tensor count of all 44 saved configs that have one exactly, once extra tensors are added back: multi-token-prediction modules (the largest: DeepSeek-V3's Hub count of 684.5B is the 671.0B main model plus a 13.5B MTP module plus 41.5M FP8 scale tensors), vision towers (Llama 4, 0.87B; Gemma 3 27B, 0.42B), buffers such as GPT-2's attention masks, and Qwen3-0.6B's stored copy of its tied head (155.6M) measured. Published headline sizes are rounded or truncated by their makers; 42 of 45 match one of three accountings, and GLM-4.5 (355B), MiniMax-M2 (230B) and Gemma 7B ("7B" for 8.54B) do not, for reasons the calculator explains.
mis_rope: Measured on the tiny GPT (RoPE, trained on 256-token windows) with the running story moved to start at position 1,024: loss 3.87 against 1.74 at position 0, and the greedy continuation turns into "friends like to play with the park was a little boy was very happy. As the sunrise, the sun came to the park." The config mistake does the same with no error: YaRN ×8 with original_max_position_embeddings set to 2,048 instead of 256 gives 3.78 at that position measured (the Past the trained length tab of Positional Encodings).
mis_lab:
• KV heads not expanded (8 query heads, 2 KV heads, PyTorch 2.14.1 SDPA without enable_gqa): RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (8) must match the size of tensor b (2) at non-singleton dimension 1.
  • Expanded with repeat instead of repeat_interleave: no error, the shapes match, but each query head reads the wrong KV head; the trained GQA-2 model's held-out loss goes from 2.103 to 2.991.
  • Keys not transposed (q @ k): RuntimeError: Expected size for first two dimensions of batch2 tensor to be: [8, 32] but got: [8, 256].
  • Learned positions past the table: IndexError: learned positions stop at 256; got position 256 (the tiny GPT raises it on purpose).
  • Silent one-line attention bugs on the trained tiny GPT, loss on the running sequence 1.96 when correct: scores not divided by √dh 2.88; heads split with .view but no transpose 3.64; heads merged without transposing back 5.03 ("Lily saw a little girl saw a little girl was the girl"); causal mask left out 3.64, and a model trained without it learns to copy the next token, held-out 0.21 with the leak and 7.02 once the mask is back (the Mask lab of Families and objectives).
  • Post-norm at the default learning rate: stuck at 5.943, the unigram loss (section 7).
  • MoE without balancing: one expert takes 48% of a layer's assignments and 14 of 48 experts get under 1% (Mixture of experts).
All measured on the laptop; errors pasted verbatim.
